- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is below recent high, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.1) and forecast is above recent high, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast to avoid overshoot.
- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes in the 3rd–5th day of a new trend — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for early trend acceleration.
- Model overestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price declines — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating ±0.15) and forecast shows sharp directional change, reduce forecast magnitude by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to short-term sentiment noise.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if forecast is 2–3% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overbought signal.
- For sentiment > 0.3 and price > 70, model often underestimates upward continuation — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for 3–5 days ahead.
- If sentiment is flat (0.0–0.1) and forecast is trending, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid false momentum.
